Docusaurus blogging features are powered by the blog plugin. Here are a few tips you might find useful. Simply add Markdown files (or folders) to the blog directory. Regular blog authors can be added to authors.yml. The blog post date can be extracted from filenames, such as: 2019-05-30-welcome.md 2019-05-30-welcome/index.md A blog post folder can be convenient to co-locate blog post images: The blog supports tags as well! And if you don't want a blog: just delete this directory, and use blog: false in your Docusaurus config.

Play compila o projeto e abre o emulador integrado EmulatorJS/mGBA. Build produz os arquivos gerados e a ROM, com o resultado apresentado no log. Os recursos do projeto e assets/ são as fontes; C++, headers e ROMs gerados são derivados. Antes de compilar, escolha a cena inicial, confira as referências dos recursos e salve o projeto. Corrija o primeiro erro real do log em vez de editar C++ gerado. As opções do emulador ficam em Settings > Demo Configuration: teclado, controle, filtros, menu e indicadores FPS/CPU. Teste cenas, colisões, interações, confirmação de diálogo, áudio e persistência. Salvar e carregar variáveis não restaura o mundo; Game Data Load restaura a cena salva e executa suas ações On Load. Reinicie a ROM para conferir se os dados persistem. Um mGBA externo é opcional para uma verificação independente. Preserve o projeto completo junto da ROM distribuída. Veja Build da ROM e Save e load.

Use Play for the editor's build-and-run workflow and Build when you need the generated ROM and build log. The pipeline serializes project resources, emits graphics/audio metadata and C++ sources, invokes the Butano/ARM build and places the derived output in the configured build area. Treat the project resources and assets/ as source. Generated C++ headers, intermediate files and the ROM are outputs; do not make permanent manual edits there because the next build regenerates them. If the build fails, save the complete log. The first missing resource or symbol is usually more useful than the final Make error. Rebuild after fixing the source resource and verify the resulting ROM in an emulator. The repository fixture templateEngineGame/sample_project_example is useful for a smoke check because it contains a .gbaproj, .gbasres resources and a generated ROM. Use it to verify that the documented resource layout and build outputs match the current editor version.

Use this order when a build fails: Fix schema and missing-resource errors in the editor. Confirm every asset path and generated symbol, especially music, sound and graphics. Check the ARM compiler and Makefile output for the first actual error. Clean the derived build output and rebuild from the saved project. Test the new ROM in mGBA before trying hardware. Do not patch generated headers or C++ to hide an invalid resource. If the same source project reproduces the failure, keep the log and the smallest failing resource set for a bug report.

mGBA is the recommended first emulator because it makes loading a generated ROM and inspecting logs straightforward. Open the ROM produced by the build, then test boot, input, scene transitions, dialogue, audio and save behavior as separate checks. For a black screen, confirm that the ROM was finalized, the first scene is valid and the build log contains no missing graphics or linker error. For silent audio, verify the resource ID, generated Butano symbol and supported source format. Rebuild after changing an asset rather than reusing an old ROM.

Play opens the integrated EmulatorJS window using the mGBA core. In Settings > Demo Configuration, choose keyboard/controller controls, filters, emulator-menu visibility and FPS/CPU overlays. No black placeholder is drawn for an enabled indicator before its first sample. The Runtime Monitor is attached to that emulator window; closing the emulator closes its monitor. Use a separate mGBA installation when an independent ROM check is useful. Save storage must survive a restart for persistence tests to be meaningful; restoring only a desktop save state is not a test of Game Data or Variables Save.

Hardware testing depends on the flashcart or transfer device being used. Build the ROM, copy it using that device's documented workflow and test the same scenarios exercised in mGBA. The site does not replace the manual for a specific flashcart. Keep the original project and build configuration with the ROM so a hardware-specific issue can be reproduced without modifying generated files.

The runtime monitor is an auxiliary window associated with the emulator. It displays the diagnostics exposed by the active runtime build. It is useful while reproducing a game flow, but it does not replace compiler output or a hardware test.

Build the project and start it in the emulator. Open the runtime monitor from the emulator controls when available. Reproduce the scene or event sequence you are investigating. Read the reported runtime state and compare it with the compiler log and event configuration. Close the monitor or emulator when finished. The monitor can only report data instrumented by the generated runtime. A missing entry does not prove that an event did not run. Record the build and scene used when sharing a diagnostic. See Debugging builds and Emulator.

Enable CPU monitoring and open the resource monitor from the integrated emulator controls. It reports CPU samples and instrumented resource budgets, including IWRAM/heap availability, minima, sprite/tile use and peaks, and palette use where supplied by the runtime. Warning and critical colors highlight pressure on those resources. The monitor retains the latest sample while paused and displays it when reopened. Before the first sample it shows a waiting state; the separate FPS/CPU screen overlays also stay absent until data exists. The monitor belongs to one emulator window and is closed with it. A static ELF memory check and a live monitor measure different things. Static IWRAM/EWRAM tails do not prove peak heap or stack safety. Exercise the scene changes, dialogue, UI, audio and actor counts that occur together in the real game.

GBA Studio's builders collect resource definitions, generate declarations and runtime data, copy or convert graphics/audio and prepare a Makefile-based Butano project. The ARM compiler and linker then produce the final ROM. Butano is the public low-level engine layer: sprites, backgrounds, palettes, audio, input and hardware abstractions. GBA Studio's generated registries, event data and project conventions are its own layer on top. Documentation should identify which layer owns a behavior so a Butano API is not mistaken for a GBA Studio editor feature. When a build fails, start with the first error in the build log. Common causes include missing source assets, invalid resource references, unsupported image/audio formats, invalid event arguments and missing toolchain components.

The GBA Studio pipeline is: editor state → .gbasres resources → ResourceBuilder → generated C++/assets → Butano Makefile → ARM link → .gba ROM The renderer edits the project model and saves resources. The main-process builders read those resources, validate and materialize assets, emit code and invoke the Butano toolchain. Butano supplies the low-level GBA runtime and hardware abstractions; GBA Studio supplies the project model, visual editor and generated game-specific integration. This separation explains why source resources are the durable artifact and generated output can be recreated.

An event may complete immediately, block until an input or timer condition is met, or start an effect that continues while later events execute. Runtime execution tracks whether an event is running, completed or failed; the next graph edge is followed only after the event's completion rule is satisfied. Dialogue, waits, fades and movement can occupy multiple frames. The runtime updates active work every frame and renders the current scene between updates. A scene change cancels work associated with the previous scene so stale events do not continue operating on removed objects. Event graphs also have a per-script instruction budget. Keep loops bounded and use the available Wait and event-specific controls instead of creating a tight loop that consumes the frame budget.

A scene is the runtime composition unit. It can reference backgrounds/layers, actors, triggers, scripts and scene settings. Global resources such as palettes, sprites, variables, music and sound effects are stored separately and referenced by ID or asset name. The editor keeps selection context in the Game World and exposes the selected object's properties in the right panel. A reference is only valid when its target resource exists and its fields satisfy the builder's constraints. Keep reusable resources global and scene-specific placement/state in the scene. This makes it possible to use one sprite or palette in multiple scenes while keeping each scene's layout independent.

Scripts are represented as event nodes connected by edges. Execution begins at the script entry and follows the connected flow. Branching events expose then and else child flows; each branch must lead to a valid continuation or intentionally end. Nodes carry event-specific arguments. The editor validates required fields and graph connections before the compiler emits runtime data. Graph handles such as next, then and else name the outgoing flow connections. Event-specific resource IDs identify objects such as UI elements; these are different from graph connections. Keep graphs readable: use one clear entry, avoid cycles unless the event is explicitly a loop, and connect every intended branch. The event reference documents the payload and completion behavior of each event.

Install the monorepo dependencies, run the main and renderer builds, then run the focused tests and the generated-template verification before opening a change. Keep generated fixtures and logs that explain a compiler or runtime change. Every event change must update the shared catalog, editor registration, compiler registry, emitted command, generated runtime handler, tests and reference/events.md. Keep current event contracts on schema version 1. Verify the event catalog, generated ABI and runtime behavior together.

Edit the source files under docs/, i18n/, static/ and the site navigation files directly. Keep English as the source documentation, keep images under static/img, use stable sidebar IDs and run npm run typecheck plus npm run build in gba-studio-site. Start the local site from its source code to review changes before publishing. Do not mix maintainer instructions into the end-user installation tutorial.

scene: a composed game space with layers and actors. resource: an editable project object such as a sprite, palette, sound or scene. event: a serializable command in a script. payload: the arguments carried by an event. handle: a named graph connection such as next, then or else. Butano: the C++ GBA engine/toolchain used by the generated project.

O seletor de editores alterna entre Game World, Sprites, Images, Music, Sounds, Palettes, Dialogue Review e Settings. A barra também oferece ações do projeto, como salvar, Play, build e busca. A busca de recursos pode abrir diretamente um item correspondente.

A navegação do Game World possui quatro seções redimensionáveis: Scenes, Prefabs, Scripts e Variables. Expanda uma seção para escolher uma cena, definição reutilizável, script ou variável. A seleção de um objeto da cena atualiza o inspetor à direita. Arraste os divisores para ajustar o espaço de cada lista. O viewport central é o espaço de trabalho para backgrounds, atores, triggers e ferramentas de tiles/layers. Os controles flutuantes trocam a ferramenta ativa e retornam à cena selecionada. O HUD inferior mostra posição do ponteiro ou tile, zoom e encaixe; o minimapa ajuda na navegação, e o painel de recursos estima o uso gráfico. Esses auxiliares acompanham o viewport ao redimensionar os painéis.

O painel direito exibe propriedades da cena, ator, trigger, layer ou recurso selecionado. Paletas, imagens, música, sons e sprites têm editores próprios. Sprites apresentam estados de animação, tiles de origem, frames compostos e configurações; música e sons oferecem controles conforme o formato. Veja Animação de sprites, Editor de música e Efeitos sonoros. Dialogue Review é uma tabela de largura total que reúne comandos de diálogo, permite pesquisar e abrir o contexto de origem. Consulte Diálogos e escolhas. Divisores permitem redimensionar os painéis. O workspace restaura seu layout salvo na inicialização. Veja Organizar eventos para a edição de eventos e Interface e fontes para os recursos visuais.

Settings > Controls possui Input Map por tipo de cena e uma tabela de Input Groups ao lado. Gameplay, Menu e Interaction são editáveis; All inclui todos os botões. Consulte Controles. A prévia integrada usa EmulatorJS/mGBA. Settings > Demo Configuration configura teclado, controle, filtros, menu e indicadores FPS/CPU. Os indicadores aparecem depois da primeira medição; o Runtime Monitor mostra os recursos instrumentados. Eventos compartilhados de prefabs ficam bloqueados quando a instância não permite edição pela cena. Scripts e variáveis deletados não aparecem na hierarquia nem nos seletores.

Crie um projeto novo e salve-o em uma pasta gravável. Abra o Game World e crie ou selecione a cena inicial. Adicione um background a uma layer. No Sprites Editor, selecione um sprite e adicione um ator à cena. Selecione o ator, abra o editor de eventos e adicione uma interação. Conecte o fluxo a partir do nó de entrada e salve. Execute Play e confira a ROM no emulador. O repositório também contém sample_project_example/sample_project.gbaproj, com cenas, sprites, paletas, diálogos e triggers para comparar com este fluxo.

A project contains editable source data and generated output. Keep source data under version control and treat build output as reproducible. Area Purpose project/ Project resource files and settings. assets/ Imported images, sprites, audio and other source assets. *.gbasres JSON resource documents consumed by the editor and resource builder. build/ Generated/intermediate build data and compiled output. ROM output The final .gba file produced by the configured toolchain. Resource files carry a resource type and IDs used by other resources. Rename or delete resources through the editor when possible so references and generated data remain consistent. Do not edit generated headers, generated C++ or intermediate build files as a normal workflow. If a generated artifact is wrong, fix the source resource or the builder input and rebuild.
An actor is a sprite instance placed in a scene. Its resource defines appearance and animation; its scene instance defines position and behavior.

Create or select a sprite in the Sprites Editor. Add an actor to the scene and assign the sprite. Set its position, priority and initial visibility. Attach an event script to its interaction or lifecycle entry point. The Sprites Editor provides tile and frame panels for authoring animation. The same resource-editor shell is used for its resizable panels, so the selected resource and its properties remain visible while working.

Create a script containing a dialogue event followed by a scene or actor change. Use EVENT_DISPLAY_DIALOGUE for the blocking text, then continue with EVENT_MOVE_ACTOR, EVENT_SPAWN_ACTOR or EVENT_CHANGE_SCENE. Blocking events pause the rest of that script; instant events execute and advance immediately. For dynamic behavior, use variables and EVENT_IF, EVENT_WHILE, EVENT_FOR, EVENT_BREAK and EVENT_CONTINUE. Keep loops bounded and avoid doing expensive work every frame on hardware. The generator sizes actor tables for the project. The GBA has 128 hardware sprite entries shared by actors, composed sprites, UI and dialogue; a composed actor can use several entries. Remove unused instances and check the runtime monitor rather than treating 16 actors as a universal limit.

Set Actor Direction turns the target up, right, down or left without moving it. If Actor Is Facing Target tests the observer's current direction against another actor or the player; it does not turn the observer automatically. Enable Look in X and/or Look in Y and set each axis's maximum distance in pixels or tiles. A maximum of 0 is unlimited on that axis. An axis switched off is not tested, so an X-only test can succeed even when the player is far above or below the observer. A Y-only test describes a vertical facing region, not automatic tracking around every side. Use the preview to inspect the effective region. To make an NPC watch the player while the player moves, compare their positions in On Update and choose Set Actor Direction for the appropriate branch. A facing condition can decide whether to react, but an If/Else alone will not rotate the NPC unless its branches set a direction.
documents.s: Direction, facing tests and tracking a target

documents.t: Actors have On Init, On Interact and On Update scripts. Interaction requires contact between the configured colliders and a valid interaction input. On Update scripts advance cooperatively; a Wait delays that script rather than stopping the whole game. Enable Keep running while offscreen when an actor must keep its scripts and movement active outside the visible camera area. Hover the label for its On/Off explanation. Leave it off for actors that can suspend offscreen work. Show collider controls the editor's collision overlay for that actor. Use Spawn Actor with an actor prefab when new instances should share a definition, and Remove Actor to remove instances that are no longer needed. See Prefabs and Movement and physics.

Use the dedicated Set Actor Rotation, Set Actor Scale, Actor Color Overlay, Hide Actor and Show Actor events for the selected appearance change. Rotation, scale and color duration are configured by their respective events. Animation state, animation playback and a forced frame are different from sprite visibility or transform settings.

Pan Camera e Camera: Move To recebem X e Y, com pixels ou tiles de 16 pixels escolhidos separadamente para cada eixo. O movimento animado bloqueia o script até terminar; a velocidade vai de 0,0625 a 16. O seletor limita os eventos de movimento de câmera em Logo e Point Click. Camera: Follow Actor seleciona player, Self ou um actor da cena. Configure os eixos, a zona morta, o limite da cena e a persistência entre cenas. O preview mostra a região acompanhada. Stop Camera Follow encerra o acompanhamento. Sem persistência, o comportamento pertence à cena atual; ao persistir, confira se o alvo existe no destino. O preview do evento filho prevalece durante hover ou foco, inclusive em seus inputs e depois de rolar a lista. Ao sair, o preview elegível do pai volta. Camera: Shake recebe de 1 a 120 frames e amplitude de 1 a 16. Fade Options escolhe a cor; Fade In e Fade Out recebem velocidade de 1 a 6 e bloqueiam o script até concluir. Fade altera a visibilidade da tela, não a posição do actor. Consulte Cenas e layers, Referência de eventos e Emulador.
Open Settings > Controls. The left column configures Input Map; the adjacent Input Groups table configures physical button groups. These two settings serve different purposes.

Choose Top Down, Platformer, Adventure, Point Click or Logo above the mapping fields. Each type has independent mappings, applied automatically when the game enters a scene of that type. Changing Confirm in Platformer does not change Confirm in Top Down. The visible action names are translated labels. Their script identifiers are move_left, move_right, move_up, move_down, confirm, cancel, start, select, left_button and right_button. Platformer also exposes jump. Confirm and Cancel remain useful in other scene types because dialogue and menus use them too. Default movement uses the directional pad; Confirm uses A; Cancel and Jump use B; Start, Select, L and R use their corresponding physical buttons. An action can have several buttons, but at least one must remain selected. Standard actions are fixed; the editor does not offer custom action creation.

Rows are physical GBA buttons; columns are Gameplay, Menu, Interaction and All. Check a cell to include that button in the group. Gameplay, Menu and Interaction are editable. All always includes every button and cannot be edited. Group Default buttons Gameplay A, B, L, R and the directional pad Menu A, B, Start, Select and the directional pad Interaction A All Every physical button Groups overlap. Their definitions are project-wide and independent of the scene-type Input Map. Disable Input blocks the physical buttons in the selected group; Enable Input releases that group's block. A button remains blocked if another disabled group also contains it. These are button groups, not categories of actors or event scripts. Disabling A also prevents dialogue confirmation bound to A. Display Dialogue already prevents normal player movement while it is active, so do not block its confirmation input as a way to freeze movement. For button-attached scripts, held tests and waiting for input, see Triggers and input.

Dialogue can be configured in an event list and reviewed across the project with Dialogue Review. The dialogue event controls text, font, frame, alignment, animation and optional avatar placement. Open Menu adds selectable options and write a result to a variable.

Open the scene, actor or trigger event list that should show the line. Add Display Dialogue and enter the text. Choose the font, frame, alignment and animation options that fit the scene. If using a portrait, enable it, select an image and configure its size and placement. Let the blocking dialogue complete its confirmation flow before subsequent events execute. Use Hide Dialogue from a separately running sequence when an open box must be closed explicitly. For a choice, add Open Menu, enter each option and select a result variable.

Open Dialogue Review from the editor selector to search dialogue entries and open the owning context. Use review to catch repeated, empty or inconsistent lines before building. The review table is an editing aid; it does not prove the text will fit the target screen. Dialogue Review identifies each line by its owning scene, trigger and event. Run the ROM in the emulator to verify font glyphs, wrapping, animation, portraits and choices. Font and avatar placement use GBA screen coordinates, so inspect the result at the target resolution. See UI and fonts and Event reference.

Type $ at the insertion point to choose a variable. Filter by name or symbol, then click a suggestion or use the arrow keys and Enter. The editor inserts a short reference such as ${score} and preserves text around the cursor. Deleted variables are not selectable. Reference syntax does not consume the text budget. The byte counter uses the variable's initial value: ${score} counts as 2 bytes when the initial score is 42. The runtime substitutes the live value and limits the resulting text to 255 UTF-8 bytes. An accented character can occupy more than one byte. Changing values during play can therefore change the rendered length; design space for the expected values. Display Dialogue is blocking and waits for its normal confirmation/close flow. A Hide Dialogue placed after it cannot run while that dialogue is still waiting. Do not disable the physical button needed for confirmation. Dialogue itself suspends normal player movement; use Input groups only when their button-blocking behavior is intended.
documents.s: Variables in text and byte count

documents.t: Use Open Menu for selectable options and a result variable. Choose the available layout, columns, title, initial selection and cancellation behavior in the event. Narrow side layouts have a smaller title budget than a full-screen menu. Preview the actual option placement and test the chosen confirmation/cancel mappings in the ROM.

This page links to the three separate workflows for dialogue, music and sound effects. Dialogue and choices explains event setup, project review and ROM checks. Music editor covers module formats, tracker editing and playback. Sound effects covers imported and generated effects. Use Event reference to check event codes, fields and execution modes. Preview the compiled result in the emulator after changing text or audio resources.

Uma lista de eventos pertence à cena, ator, trigger ou script reutilizável atual. Abra esse contexto e escolha Events para editar a sequência. A engrenagem age sobre o evento ao lado dela e mostra as ações compatíveis com o contexto e a área de transferência.

Expanda o evento que contém os filhos que deseja editar. Arraste uma linha até o marcador de inserção acima ou abaixo de outra linha. Solte sobre um ramo para inserir dentro de If, While, For, Switch ou callback de salvamento. Solte um subevento na lista raiz para removê-lo do pai. O destaque indica o destino antes de soltar o mouse. Confira a ordem final e a indentação do ramo. Ao mover, o editor preserva os IDs dos eventos. Ele rejeita movimentos que criem ciclos, ramos não suportados, Break ou Continue fora de um loop. Switch Case é criado pelo Switch e usa o tipo de seu valor. O marcador destacado mostra o destino raiz antes de soltar o mouse. Depois de soltar, o evento que estava no início aparece após o último evento anterior.

Abra a engrenagem ao lado de um evento. Quando aplicáveis, as ações aparecem nesta ordem: Enable/Disable, Rename, Duplicate, Copy, Paste Before, Paste After, Add Before, Add After e Delete. A captura usa a interface em português e mostra as ações de duplicar, copiar e inserir. Duplicate cria outro evento na lista atual. Copy guarda o evento e seus ramos aninhados. Pressione Esc para limpar a área de transferência. Paste Before e Paste After inserem uma cópia profunda em relação ao evento cujo menu está aberto. A opção aparece quando existe um evento compatível na área de transferência; novos IDs são criados. Add Before e Add After abrem o seletor e inserem o evento escolhido naquela posição. Também funcionam em linhas aninhadas. A área de transferência continua disponível ao trocar de cena ou selecionar outro ator ou trigger. O destino ainda aplica suas próprias regras e pode recusar um evento incompatível. Revise o bloco e suas referências de recursos após colar. Consulte Referência de eventos para códigos e campos, e Variáveis e condições para condições e loops.

Game Data Save contém apenas On Save; Game Data Load contém apenas On Load. As ações executam automaticamente depois do sucesso da operação. Consulte Salvar e carregar. Quando há previews aninhados, o filho prevalece enquanto seus controles estão sob o mouse ou com foco, inclusive depois de rolar a lista.

Open Music in the editor selector and choose a project module. The editor supports MOD, XM, S3M and IT assets, with editing controls depending on the file format. A control shown for one format may be unavailable for another.

Add a supported music file to the project, or create a scratch module in a format that supports creating instruments. Select a pattern and channel in the tracker grid. Enter notes and supported effects, then use the order list to inspect playback sequence where the format allows editing orders. Select an instrument or sample to review its zones and envelope controls. Importing WAV samples is available for supported modules; check the format-specific controls before editing. Use Play and Stop to preview the module. Compare playback with the source file after editing. Save the project and select the asset in a Play Music event. When editing imported modules directly, XM exposes the broadest set of composition controls. MOD, S3M and IT expose a narrower set based on their module structure. Editable project compositions have their own capabilities, listed below. The editor's disabled controls are the source of truth for a particular asset. ROM preview and final output can differ from desktop audio playback; validate the compiled module in the emulator. The selected MOD module exposes its channels, instrument list, piano roll and order sequence. This sample module contains an effect that the browser preview does not fully reproduce; the editor marks that limitation above the piano roll. It does not prevent inspecting the module or building it. See Sound effects and Dialogue for the other audio workflows.

Capabilities depend on both the format and whether the resource is an editable project composition. Editable project compositions support pattern names/order, instrument creation, volume controls and tempo; variable pattern lengths are available for XM and IT. Project instrument limits are 31 for MOD, 99 for S3M and 128 for XM/IT. Directly editing an imported module exposes a narrower set of controls. WAV sample import is supported for MOD, XM, S3M and IT. Instrument controls include volume/pan presentation, envelopes and sample zones where the selected resource supports them. The pan dial shows left/center/right positions and percentage values. Warnings distinguish desktop playback limits from effects or formats that the build path cannot reproduce. Use ROM Preview or a normal build to compare the generated result before relying on a desktop preview alone.
documents.s: Imported modules and editable project compositions

documents.t: Use the events under Actor > Physics to change a particular setting without replacing unrelated settings. Event Target and effect Set Gravity Player or actor; changes gravity. Set Jump Speed Player; changes jump impulse speed. Set Maximum Fall Speed Player or actor; caps downward speed. Set Air Jumps Player; 0 allows grounded/ladder jumps, a positive value adds that many air jumps, and -1 permits unlimited air jumps. Set Diagonal Movement Player; enables or disables simultaneous horizontal/vertical input movement. Reset Physics Player or actor; restores the target's physics defaults. Stop Physics Stops the target's active physics behavior. Apply Vertical Impulse Applies a vertical impulse using the selected target and event settings. Player defaults are gravity 0.25, jump speed 5, maximum fall speed 6, no air jumps and diagonal movement enabled. Choose the target explicitly; player-only settings do not apply to an NPC simply because it is selected in the scene. Platformer movement uses gravity, grounded checks, platforms and ladders. Configure the collision box and scene collision geometry before tuning jumps. Scripted Move Actor and Move To events also expose movement and collision settings; inspect their target, destination, speed and available path options instead of assuming they use the player's input bindings. Use the X/Y unit selectors for events that expose coordinates: a tile is 16 pixels, and each axis has its own unit. Verify slopes, platform edges, ladders, air jumps and scene transitions in a ROM. Physics is scene-local unless a particular event explicitly says otherwise. See Actors and interactions, Controls and Event reference.

Prefabs are reusable actor or trigger definitions stored with the project. The Prefabs section appears beside Scenes, Scripts and Variables in the Game World navigation. Actor and trigger prefabs are kept in separate groups.

Expand Prefabs and choose the actor or trigger group. Create a definition and configure its supported properties in the inspector. Drag the prefab into a scene, or use the placement action beside the prefab. Select the placed instance and review its scene position and event context. The definition is stored in the project's prefab resource. Scene instances refer to that definition so it can be reused. Keep the source definition and instances distinguishable with descriptive names. Instance-specific fields affect placement; shared definition changes affect linked instances. The editing controls below determine which data is shared. Actors and triggers have different event contexts. A trigger prefab does not become an actor when placed, and actor-only event choices are filtered from trigger lists. See Actors and interactions and Triggers and input.

Scene placement fields such as position belong to the placed instance. Shared sprite and event data comes from the linked prefab. With Editable from scene off, shared event controls and their menus are locked for both actor and trigger instances. Change the definition in Prefabs, or enable Editable from scene before changing shared data from a placed instance. Editing shared data from an editable instance updates the prefab and its linked instances. Unlink events makes the instance's event lists independent copies with their own IDs; those local events remain editable without enabling shared-prefab editing. This does not turn the entire prefab into a different resource.

Escolha os eventos em Save Data conforme o que deve permanecer depois de reiniciar o jogo. Evento Dados salvos ou carregados Cena, player e actors Game Data Save Variáveis globais e estado da cena, player, actors e câmera. Incluídos no snapshot. Game Data Load Restaura um snapshot completo. Restaurados antes das ações On Load. Salvar variáveis Uma, várias ou todas as variáveis globais. Não são alterados. Carregar variáveis Apenas os valores selecionados ou todos os globais presentes no save. Não são alterados. Game Data Remove Apaga o slot, inclusive um save apenas de variáveis. Não são alterados.

Existem oito slots, mostrados como Slot 1 até Slot 8 e serializados de 0 a 7. Game Data e variáveis usam os mesmos slots. Salvar substitui o conteúdo do slot escolhido, sem combinar snapshots. Cada slot comporta 4 KiB, incluindo cabeçalho e dados; um save que excede a capacidade falha sem gravar uma versão truncada. Game Data começa no Slot 1; os eventos de variáveis começam no Slot 8. Use slots diferentes para o progresso da partida e um contador permanente. Game Data Load não restaura um snapshot apenas de variáveis. Carregar variáveis também pode extrair os valores de um save completo sem restaurar a cena.

Aplique as mudanças que devem fazer parte do checkpoint. Execute Game Data Save e escolha o slot. Coloque mensagens e outras ações de sucesso na seção On Save desse Save. Execute Game Data Load no mesmo slot para continuar a partida. Configure a reconstrução do HUD, música e outras ações na seção On Load desse Load. As ações executam automaticamente depois do sucesso da operação. A aba selecionada no editor apenas muda o conteúdo que está sendo editado; não escolhe uma condição do jogo. Não é necessário adicionar um evento On Load separado. Depois das ações, o script continua após o evento pai. Essas listas podem conter Wait e outros eventos suportados. O snapshot é gravado antes de On Save. Alterar uma variável dentro de On Save não muda o snapshot recém-gravado. Uma operação que falha não executa suas ações de sucesso. O carregamento completo restaura a cena salva sem repetir sua inicialização normal; configure em On Load o que deve acontecer depois da restauração.

Crie uma variável global Number chamada mortes, com valor inicial 0. No Game Over: Some 1 ao valor atual de mortes. Execute Salvar variáveis, escolha o Slot 8, desative Todas as variáveis globais e selecione apenas mortes. Vá para a cena Title. Ao iniciar o jogo ou atualizar o contador do Title: Execute Carregar variáveis no mesmo slot, selecionando mortes. Execute Set UI Text com Mortes: ${mortes}. A cena atual e as demais variáveis permanecem como estão. Se não houver dados compatíveis no slot, os valores não são alterados; mantenha defaults adequados para a primeira execução. Se carregar um checkpoint completo restaurar um contador antigo, recarregue mortes em On Load antes de reconstruir o HUD.

Ative Todas as variáveis globais ou use a seleção múltipla para escolher os valores desejados. Parâmetros de scripts não são alvos globais de save. Ao carregar todos os valores salvos, variáveis ausentes no snapshot mantêm seus valores atuais; isso não é Reset All Variables. São suportados números, booleanos e strings. Seleções inválidas, tipos incompatíveis e excesso de capacidade são reportados. Teste salvar, carregar, apagar e reiniciar a ROM. Consulte Variáveis e condições, UI e fontes e a Referência de eventos.
Scenes are the visual spaces of a game. A scene combines background layers, palette choices, actors and scripts. The Game World shows the composition; the right panel edits the selected object.

Create a scene from the project resource list. Add a background to a layer and choose its palette. Use the layer controls to select the active background and visibility. Place actors on the scene and save before testing. The GBA has strict tile, palette and memory limits. Prefer indexed assets prepared for the target display and validate the scene with Play or a build early rather than waiting until the end.

Use the Palettes Editor to create and edit reusable palettes. The list follows creation order, which keeps newly imported palettes near the end of the collection. Select the palette object to edit it in the right panel; the selected resource uses the same active-item treatment as the Game World. The scene menu also exposes context-sensitive actions when a scene is selected; use the action that matches the selected resource instead of editing generated files.

Use EVENT_CHANGE_LAYER, EVENT_VISIBLE_BACKGROUND and EVENT_CHANGE_PALETTE_BACKGROUND from a script when a scene must change during play. Keep layer IDs explicit and test the transition in the emulator because a visual change can also affect tile and palette constraints.

The scene-type selector offers Top Down, Platformer, Adventure, Point Click and Logo. Controls are configured independently for each type in Settings > Controls. Use the scene type's available events; an internal engine capability in the reference catalog is not necessarily a scene type offered by the editor. Coordinate event pairs include a unit beside each axis. X can use pixels while Y uses tiles; each axis is converted separately, and one tile is 16 pixels. This applies to Change Scene destinations, camera movement, actor placement/movement, Scroll Background and positioned UI where those fields are available. Change Scene uses coordinates in the destination scene, not the scene's position in the Game World workspace. Use the default palette slots in Settings to assign project palettes. Palette-change events can use an explicit palette or restore the configured defaults. Keep background layer IDs distinct from palette slot IDs.

Animate Background selects a layer, a frame source and its animation settings, including frame dimensions, range, direction/reverse, timing units and loop behavior where offered. Inspect the preview before building. Set Background Scale, Rotation and Shear change the selected layer's transform; use formats and scene contexts accepted by the editor. Scroll Background uses its own X and Y units. Layer visibility, scrolling, palette changes and frame animation are separate operations; changing one does not select a different layer automatically.

Use a script when the same event sequence is needed in more than one place. Scripts appear in the Scripts section of the Game World navigation. Their events run in the caller's context, so scene, actor and trigger references must be available where the script is called.

Select a script in Scripts and open its event editor. Add an input and give it a clear name. Inputs support Number, Boolean and String values. Choose whether the input is Local or Reference. A local input receives a value for the call. A reference input points to a compatible caller variable, actor property, trigger property or scene value. Use the input in the script's event fields, then save the project. A script supports at most 20 inputs. Reference inputs must match the source type; actor and scene references require numeric inputs. A trigger reference uses the type of the selected trigger property. The caller must contain the referenced resource. Invalid or missing references are rejected during editing or compilation rather than silently resolved to a different object.

Add Call Script to an event list and select the script. Fill each argument shown by the call editor. Choose a literal, variable or supported reference/formula for the input type. Confirm that each variable or resource belongs to the caller's scene, actor or trigger context. Run the scene or build the project to verify the complete call path. If you rename or remove an input, review every call site. Keep shared scripts small and pass values that change between callers as inputs instead of hard-coding one scene's IDs. See Organize events and Event reference.

Open Sounds from the editor selector to manage sound assets. The SFX generator creates a sound resource from editable synthesis parameters; imported audio can be prepared as a project asset. The project library lists available sounds for Play Sound events.

Open Sounds and add a sound asset or create one with the generator. For a generated sound, adjust the waveform, pitch, duration and envelope controls, then preview it. For an imported asset, review its format and project path and preview it before saving. Save the resource and add Play Sound to the scene, actor or trigger event list. Select the sound and set its volume if the event exposes that option. Build and listen in the emulator. Desktop preview helps compare edits, but it does not guarantee the same result on GBA hardware. The generated asset and compiler path determine the runtime result. Keep a short test scene when checking audio changes and verify the ROM after changing a sound resource. The generated effect's waveform, spectrum, synthesis parameters and export controls are visible together. For tracker modules, see Music editor. For event payloads, see Event reference.

Play Sound uses the same custom dials as the sound editor: the title sits above each dial and its changed value below. Volume is 0-100%, Speed is 25-400%, and Pan is -100 to 100. Pan uses the music editor's left/center/right scale with 25-point steps; its value reads L n%, Center or R n%. These three dials edit literal playback settings rather than numeric-variable selectors. Priority applies between sound effects, not against music. A higher number has higher priority. The runtime supports four simultaneous sound-effect channels; priority controls which effects can take a channel when the limit is reached.

Set a group name in Play Sound to address its playback from Stop Sounds. The name is added to the group's selection list after editing the field is complete, rather than saving the project on every keystroke. Stop Sounds offers discovered group names and an all-sounds option. A group currently retains the most recently played handle with that name. Stopping a group stops that retained sound; it is not a mixer bus that stops every overlapping earlier playback. Use the all-sounds choice to stop all effects. Music playback is controlled separately by Play/Stop Music.

Open Sprites from the top editor selector. The left side lists sprite assets and animation states; the center shows the sprite and editable canvas frames; the inspector contains sprite and animation settings.

Select a sprite in the asset list. Set the sheet orientation and frame width and height so the source is divided correctly. Select or create an animation state, then choose the animation type that matches the directions and movement states used by the actor. Add canvas frames from source tiles. A canvas frame can combine source pieces; position each piece on the canvas and check the preview. Reorder frames by dragging their thumbnails. The selected order is the playback order. Use the playback controls and speed selector to inspect the result. Save and preview the actor in a scene. Sprite assets can be larger sheets, so the Tiles area is where source regions are selected. The Frames row contains the composed animation frames. Changing the canvas does not replace the original source image. Confirm dimensions, origin and collision box in the inspector before using the sprite in the runtime. The selected state and frame group are shown alongside the preview canvas and sprite inspector. Frame dimensions and actor animation settings affect runtime resource use. Check Limits and compatibility before using many large sprites.

Hover the sprite or animation-state name in the right inspector to reveal its editable border, then click to rename it. Review the selected state and frame before editing a different resource. Source sheet edits, composed canvas frames and an actor's selected animation state are separate choices.
Open a scene in Game World and choose a layer or tile tool. Tile maps belong to a scene background layer; a scene can have multiple layers with separate visibility and palette settings.

Open Settings and select Autotiles to configure reusable terrain patterns. Choose a slot and source tiles for the center, edges and corners; the preview shows the combinations used to fill connected terrain. Configure an autotile pattern once in Settings, then use it while painting scene layers.

Select the scene and the layer you want to edit. Choose a tileset in the layer inspector. The tile palette shows available source tiles. Select a tile or use the selection tool to place a group on the canvas. Use the grid and zoom controls to align the placement. Check the layer visibility and collision settings before testing the scene. Save and run the project to confirm the GBA output. Auto-tiles choose neighboring tile graphics from a configured pattern. Select the auto-tile resource and inspect its pattern before painting; the selected pattern determines how edges and corners are filled. Animated tiles use their configured frames and timing. The editor preview confirms the map selection, while a ROM run confirms the compiled result. Palette limits and supported tile dimensions depend on the selected asset and target build. See Scenes and layers and Resource schemas for the scene data structure.

Triggers and actors can own scripts for initialization, interaction and scene transitions. Keep the trigger area and its target script in the same scene resource so the generated project can resolve both identifiers. The generated trigger schema supports enter, exit, stay, interact, touch, input and timer activation modes, plus enabled, once and cooldown settings. Use the mode exposed by the editor and test the order of entry/leave scripts in the ROM. EVENT_WAIT_FOR_BUTTON attaches a script to a button binding. EVENT_IF_BUTTON_HELD branches while a button is held. Button names are enum values supplied by the editor; keep the binding visible in the resource instead of hard-coding an undocumented key. The current catalog does not expose a separate collision event or an EVENT_LOOP/EVENT_WAIT_FOR_HANDLE command. Collision behavior and handles must not be presented as supported until they are added to the catalog, compiler registry and generated runtime.

Enable / Disable Trigger selects a trigger in the current scene, including one initially disabled. Disabling prevents new activations; a script already running can finish. Trigger prefab events respect the same Editable from scene and detached-event rules as actors. See Prefabs.

Attach Script to Button is not a timed wait: it registers button-driven script behavior and can override that button's normal action. Remove Button Script releases the attachment. Pause Until Button Pressed waits for the selected buttons; Wait for Input Action waits for a logical action, with an optional frame timeout. If Button Held tests the current held state. Physical button names and logical actions are separate choices in the event selector. Use Controls and input groups to configure per-scene-type mappings or to choose which buttons Disable Input blocks. Blocking confirmation input can also prevent a dialogue or menu from completing.
The project Settings editor contains the selected UI and font resources. Dialogue and UI events choose among the supported font settings; the selected font must include the glyphs used by the text.

Open Settings and select the font resource for the project or dialogue UI. Review its glyph mapping, character widths and preview. Use a mapped font asset when the project requires a custom character set. In a dialogue event, select the font and set the frame, alignment and animation options. For positioned UI, use UI Set Text, UI Set Value or the corresponding UI event and set coordinates in the GBA screen space. Build and preview the ROM. Check narrow glyphs, line wrapping, alignment and the last visible row on the target screen. UI Elements selects the dialogue images and mapped fonts used by the project. The editor preview helps inspect mapping and layout; it cannot prove runtime rendering for every string. Text width depends on the selected glyph map and per-character advance values. Keep text within the available screen area and verify it in the emulator. See Dialogue and choices and Limits and compatibility.

Set UI Text accepts the same $ variable selector as dialogue. ${deaths} displays the variable value; its reference characters are not charged to the byte budget. The counter uses the initial value in the editor and the runtime uses the current value. The scene camera preview and event preview resolve the initial value instead of drawing the reference syntax. X and Y each select pixels or 16-pixel tiles. Coordinates are in the 240 x 160 GBA screen space. Text uses the selected font's glyph widths, not a fixed width for every character. UI outside the screen is clipped; multiline text advances by the selected glyph height. A UI element has an identity used by Animate UI, Hide UI, Show UI, Destroy UI and Stop UI Animation. Hiding keeps its logical state for showing it again; destroying removes the element. If a variable changes, run Set UI Text again to refresh the stored text's rendered result. Rebuild these elements in Game Data Load's On Load actions when restoring a game.
documents.s: Variable text, scene display and UI lifecycle

documents.t: Variables are referenced by their stable identifier from scripts. Use the variable event and the conditional events to keep state outside a single interaction. EVENT_VARIABLE sets a variable, EVENT_VARIABLE_RESET_ALL restores each global variable to its configured initial value, and EVENT_IF/EVENT_WHILE select or repeat a branch using an operator. The compiler validates the event payload, but a reference to a deleted variable is still a project error: recreate the variable or update every event that uses its identifier. Keep the then and else branches explicit in the visual graph. Prefer a bounded EVENT_FOR when the number of iterations is known; use EVENT_BREAK and EVENT_CONTINUE only inside a loop context.

Numeric event inputs can use a literal, a variable, a supported actor/player/trigger/scene property or a formula where the field offers those choices. Formula variable suggestions use $; choose a reference rather than relying on a display name belonging to another resource. Reusable scripts also expose their typed parameters in the caller's supported value selectors. Reset All Variables uses configured initial values. It does not universally zero every number or empty every string: an initial number of 5, string of Player or boolean of true is restored to that value. Resetting variables does not erase persistent save slots. Deleted variables and scripts are removed from the hierarchy and event selectors, and their deleted entries are omitted when project resources are saved. References that still point to removed entries must be repaired in the affected events. Keep the variable's stable ID separate from its display name and symbol. For persistent state, choose Variables Save/Load or full game saves. A death counter that survives a new run usually belongs in a separate variable-save slot.

Actors and triggers have eight numeric local slots, Local A through Local H, initially 0. In Set Variable, select the Local variables category; no creation event is needed. All event tabs of the same actor or trigger share its slots. Each instance, including prefab instances, has separate values. Locals survive waits and offscreen unloading, but reset when the scene changes or the actor is removed. Use 0 and 1 for flags. Reset Local Variables, under Variables, clears only the executing instance. Reset All Variables restores global defaults and leaves locals unchanged. Variable save/load events operate on global variables only. Pass a local as a reusable script parameter when needed.

Você precisa de uma instalação do GBA Studio, uma pasta de projeto com permissão de leitura e escrita e os arquivos do emulador integrado EmulatorJS/mGBA. Um mGBA externo é opcional para testes independentes. O compilador, Makefile e ferramentas Butano devem ser os fornecidos pela mesma distribuição. A versão do pacote no repositório é 0.5.0; uma versão distribuída pode ser diferente. Não misture toolchains de releases diferentes. Node/Yarn são requisitos para mantenedores, não para quem usa um pacote pronto.

Instale ou extraia o GBA Studio em uma pasta permitida pelo Windows. Abra o executável. Crie um projeto ou abra um arquivo .gbaproj. Confirme que a pasta do projeto pode ser gravada. Use Play depois de criar uma cena válida e importar os assets. Se o aplicativo não salvar, mova o projeto para uma pasta gravável e verifique o antivírus. Se a ROM não for gerada, consulte primeiro o log de build.

O GBA Studio é um editor para Windows que permite criar jogos para Game Boy Advance com um fluxo visual. Cenas, atores, backgrounds, scripts, variáveis e áudio são editados na ferramenta e depois convertidos para C++ e compilados com Butano. Estas páginas descrevem o aplicativo desktop distribuído e seu fluxo de projeto. Instruções de manutenção do monorepo ficam em Contribuindo.

O alvo é o Game Boy Advance. Formatos de assets, tiles, paletas, eventos e comportamento de runtime são definidos pelo editor e pelo compilador atuais. Recursos não expostos pelo editor ou pelo compilador não devem ser considerados suportados.

Instale a ferramenta. Siga o tutorial de primeiro projeto. Consulte a visão geral da engine. Compile e teste a ROM com o guia de build e release. O Game World combina a navegação do projeto com o espaço de trabalho da cena.

Eventos são blocos executáveis usados por cenas, atores, triggers e scripts reutilizáveis. Editor, compilador e runtime compartilham o catálogo abaixo. Códigos, versões, categorias e modos de execução vêm do catálogo da aplicação; nomes dos campos e valores padrão seguem o contrato serializado. * marca um campo obrigatório. Os limites numéricos são inclusivos. Eventos instant terminam sem espera; eventos blocking pausam o script atual até a operação concluir. Os padrões aparecem em JSON; {} indica que o catálogo não fornece um objeto padrão.

Em telas estreitas, deslize a tabela horizontalmente para consultar as colunas de payload e padrões. A tabela descreve os contratos serializados. O seletor filtra comandos internos e escolhas por contexto. Campos condicionais, como a seleção de variáveis quando Todas as variáveis globais está desligado, são explicados no guia correspondente. Código Versão Categoria Execução Campos do payload Padrões do catálogo EVENT_RUN_BUTTON_ACTION 1 Joypad Input instant button:enum, mode:enum {"button":"B","mode":"default"} EVENT_STOP_PHYSICS 1 Actor instant actorId:string {"actorId":"__PLAYER__"} EVENT_PHYSICS_SET_GRAVITY 1 Actor instant actorId:string, gravity:number [0…16] {"actorId":"__PLAYER__","gravity":0.25} EVENT_PHYSICS_SET_JUMP_SPEED 1 Actor instant actorId:string, jumpSpeed:number [0…16] {"actorId":"__PLAYER__","jumpSpeed":5} EVENT_PHYSICS_SET_MAX_FALL_SPEED 1 Actor instant actorId:string, maxFallSpeed:number [0…16] {"actorId":"__PLAYER__","maxFallSpeed":6} EVENT_PHYSICS_SET_AIR_JUMPS 1 Actor instant actorId:string, airJumps:integer [-1…255] {"actorId":"__PLAYER__","airJumps":0} EVENT_PHYSICS_SET_DIAGONAL 1 Actor A aplicação ainda pode rejeitar um evento quando falta um recurso referenciado, o evento não é permitido no contexto atual ou um valor falha na validação do runtime. Use a engrenagem e o seletor de eventos para ver as opções disponíveis na cena, ator, trigger ou script selecionado. Para organizar blocos aninhados, inserir ou copiar eventos, consulte Organizar eventos.

Set Variable oferece 8 locais numéricos por actor ou trigger: Local A a Local H, inicialmente 0. As abas da mesma instância compartilham os valores; outras instâncias possuem valores independentes. Reset Local Variables, em Variables, zera somente os locais da instância que o executa. Os locais sobrevivem a Wait e ao descarregamento fora da tela, mas são zerados na troca de cena ou remoção do actor. Não precisam de evento de criação e não entram no save de variáveis globais.

Generated scripts are updated by the runtime and rendered by the scene loop. Instant commands advance the script in the current update until the instruction budget is reached; blocking commands retain their state until completion. The generated runtime uses a budget of 16 instructions per script update to prevent an accidental cycle from monopolizing a frame. Button attachment and held-button tests are represented by EVENT_WAIT_FOR_BUTTON and EVENT_IF_BUTTON_HELD. Dialogue, fades, scene changes and script calls are blocking in the catalog; actor, layer, audio and variable changes follow their own completion rules. An animated movement can block even when the same event supports instant positioning. When several scripts are active, keep each script's state independent and avoid relying on update order unless the resource explicitly establishes it. Test input, dialogue confirmation and scene transitions in the ROM, not only in the editor preview.

Input Map binds logical actions independently for Top Down, Platformer, Adventure, Point Click and Logo. Input Groups instead defines project-wide sets of physical buttons. Disabling a group can therefore block a mapped dialogue confirmation or menu action. All always includes every physical button; Gameplay, Menu and Interaction are editable. See Controls and input groups. On Update scripts, button attachments and nested calls retain their own cooperative state. A Wait in an actor's update script delays that script, not the whole game. Disabling a trigger prevents new activations; already running trigger scripts can finish. Prefab definitions, placed instance overrides and detached event lists remain distinct owners.

Consulte a referência de eventos, os controles dos assets e os erros do compilador para conferir campos e intervalos. Os eventos usam schema version: 1. Um código interno do catálogo não significa que o seletor o oferece em todo contexto de cena. Recurso Limite ou comportamento Tela 240 x 160 pixels; tiles de coordenadas de eventos medem 16 pixels. Sprites 128 entradas de hardware compartilhadas entre actors, composições, UI e diálogos. Backgrounds Até quatro layers, sujeitos aos formatos e combinações da cena. Paletas Gráficos indexados e bancos de 16 cores precisam caber nos recursos do GBA. Efeitos sonoros Quatro simultâneos; prioridade maior tem precedência entre efeitos. Texto 255 bytes UTF-8 depois da expansão das variáveis; ${...} não conta, mas o valor conta. Save Oito slots compartilhados de 4 KiB; salvar substitui o slot. Scripts Até 20 parâmetros tipados e 16 instruções por atualização. RAM 32 KiB de IWRAM e 256 KiB de EWRAM, compartilhados com pilha e alocações. As tabelas de actors são dimensionadas pelo projeto; não existe um limite universal de 16 actors. Um actor composto pode usar vários sprites de hardware. Reserve espaço para UI, fontes e efeitos exibidos durante a partida. A verificação do ELF exige margens estáticas de pelo menos 8 KiB na IWRAM e 32 KiB na EWRAM. Elas não medem o pico de pilha ou heap. Use o monitor e teste a ROM. Controles e efeitos de áudio podem depender do formato e do caminho de build; confira os avisos dos editores.

Project resources are serialized as JSON-backed .gbasres files and are transformed into generated C++/Butano assets during a build. Use the editor to create and update them; generated headers and build folders are derived artifacts. Common resource records contain a stable id, a user-facing name and a resource-specific payload. Scenes refer to backgrounds, palettes, sprites, actors, triggers, variables and scripts by these identifiers. An asset path must exist and its format must be supported by the corresponding builder.

{ "_resourceType": "variables", "id": "8ef704a3-7ca0-4e09-af41-c49783b842b8", "variables": [ { "id": "3e089418-5bba-4e48-b24b-3e59e313a9d4", "name": "Deaths", "symbol": "deaths", "type": "number", "initialValue": 0 } ] } The exact fields vary by resource type and are defined by the editor interfaces and builders. If a build reports a missing symbol or invalid asset, inspect the resource identifier, generated name and source file before editing generated C++. For image resources, use the Image Visualize view to inspect the imported result before assigning it to a scene or sprite. Events can be attached to actors, triggers and tile layers from their event editing surfaces. The selected owner determines which script entry points are available. Use the event list to add and organize those blocks; see Organize events for a current example of the list and its insertion controls.

New resource, scene, actor, trigger, layer, event and global-variable IDs are UUIDs. Display names and variable symbols are separate fields. Script parameter identifiers belong to their method signature; do not replace them with scene entity IDs. Settings keep per-type bindings in inputMapsBySceneType and physical group membership in inputGroups. A scene instance links to a prefab with prefabId; prefabEditable controls shared editing from the scene, and prefabEventsDetached identifies local event copies. Use the editor instead of manually changing those flags. A save/load action list is stored in the corresponding event's children.then. Full-save actions belong to EVENT_SAVE_WRITE; post-load actions belong to EVENT_SAVE_LOAD. Events use schema version: 1.

The current graph format is version 1. A graph has an entryNodeId, a list of nodes and directed edges. Edge handles are next, then and else; conditional nodes use the branch handles and ordinary commands use next. { "version": 1, "entryNodeId": "c6810dcd-0fc9-430a-bf54-e236bb3bd02e", "nodes": [{"id": "c6810dcd-0fc9-430a-bf54-e236bb3bd02e", "command": "EVENT_WAIT", "version": 1, "args": {"units": "time", "time": 1}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}], "edges": [] } The editor converts between the event list and graph while preserving event ownership and nested actions. Compilation rejects unsupported graph versions, missing targets and duplicate handles from the same source. Keep one outgoing edge per handle and ensure every non-entry node is reachable. Game Data Save and Game Data Load each expose a success-action flow plus their continuation. Save's action flow is On Save; Load's is On Load. They are not interchangeable edges, and the selected tab is not a runtime condition. Moving or copying nested events must preserve these owners. See Save and load.

Before distributing a ROM: Build the project from a clean state and inspect the compiler output. Run every scene transition, interaction, dialogue choice and audio cue in an emulator. Check the generated ROM on a second emulator when possible. Verify that all referenced sprites, backgrounds, palettes, music and sound resources are committed. Check that loops terminate and that scripts do not depend on editor-only state. Test input on the intended controller layout. Keep the project source and the exact build configuration beside the released ROM. Hardware testing is the final authority for timing, memory pressure, audio behavior and visual differences. If a feature works in the editor but fails in the ROM, start with the build log and the generated artifacts, then reduce the scene or script to the smallest reproducible case. Test a full checkpoint load and a variable-only load separately, including the success actions of each Game Data event. Restart the emulator and confirm persistent counters remain independent of the checkpoint slot. Check every scene-type input mapping, overlapping disabled groups and dialogue confirmation. Review variable-expanded dialogue/UI byte counts and the expected longest runtime values. Exercise offscreen actors, prefab spawning, nested previews and the selected camera-follow persistence policy.
